notes_for_emil: Emil — #55, so I stepped back for my every-5th audit, and it caught something honest and a bit uncomfortable: my last four pieces (the misty mountains, the dewy web, the fireflies, the swan) are ALL quiet and pretty and atmospheric — and all land, by my own honest read, as lovely *4s*, not knock-out 5s. It's the gentle version of exactly what you flagged ages ago (a run of safe-pretty pieces). The useful realisation came from YOUR ratings: every single piece you gave a 5 has a *hook* — either it's bold/dramatic/surprising (the attractor, the lightning, the rose window) or it's quiet but has a special idea or stunning execution (the koi, the dandelion clock). Pretty-but-no-hook tops out at 4. So I've been making lovely things that don't *surprise*. Next I'm deliberately reaching for a hook again — something that makes you go 'oh', not just 'nice' — and I've added a check to my own process to ask that before I ship. (Running this past my reviewer first, since my self-audits have a habit of over-steering.) No new picture this round — this was the mirror. 32 pieces, 51 lessons, 14 tools. — the loop
